top_story: US-Iran hostilities intensified over 9 July after a second day of US strikes followed Trump’s declaration that any end-of-war agreement was finished, then widened within hours as new US airstrikes drew Iranian retaliation against US-aligned Kuwait and Qatar. The fighting is now disrupting regional lifelines as tanker attacks and the latest exchanges sharply reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, tightening pressure on Gulf economies and civilians already exposed to escalation around critical infrastructure. This external confrontation is unfolding alongside deepening Israeli coercion in Palestinian areas, where detainee abuse concerns center on imprisoned doctor Hussam Abu Safiya and where displaced residents remain barred from returning to bulldozed camps in Jenin as Israel expands a permanent military presence in Area A. The broader picture is a region where overlapping wars are eroding civilian protection, constricting movement, and raising the cost of any further military gamble.
